messages.body_plain:
Hi,

there are two issues:
- there are 9 runs x 10 channels = 90 unique rows required in annotation, but the annotation I got has 100 rows -> use unique(annotation) rather than annotation
- columns in your input are called Abundance 126 etc, so MSstats assumes channels named 126, 130N etc. These are the channel IDs it extracts from PSM report. Your annotation should have these values in the Channel column, not channel.1, channel.2 etc that are currently there.

Please let me know if it solves your problems

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.subject: Re: MSstat via Skyline
messages.body_plain:
I think the thing which is confusing MSstats is that one of the folders in your path starts with a number ("23308834").
The problem is that "\2" has a special meaning in regular expressions.

The latest version of the MSstats external tool in Skyline was written by me. I think I will be able to fix this error by replacing the backslashes with forward slashes before calling MSstats to save the graphs.

Thank you for reporting this bug. I will try to fix it soon. For now, you can probably work around this bug by saving your Skyline document in a different folder where none of the parent folder names in the full path start with a number.
-- Nick

Hi,

Protein: protein ID
Label: names of Conditions selected for comparisons separated by "vs"
log2FC: log-fold change between conditions listed in the "Label" column estimated by MSstats [basically ANOVA]

DF: degrees of freedom of the distribution of test statistics
pvalue: p-value calculated based on the T-statistic
adj.pvalue: p-value adjusted for multiple comparisons using Benjamini-Hochberg method
issue: lists possible issues such as MSstats not being able to produce a p-value due to lack of biological replicates
MissingPercentage and ImputationPercentage: percentage of missing values and imputed values, respectively, in feature-level data used to produce the protein-level data that was then used to produce these testing results

Hope this helps, don't hesitate to let us know if you need additional information.

Kind regards,
Mateusz Staniak

messages.subject: issue with direction (sign) of infinite regulation
messages.subject_clean: issue with direction (sign) of infinite regulation
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstatsTeam

We've recently observed an issue with MSstats groupComparison function resulting in a wrong direction of inifinite FC depending on ordering of contrast matrix:

I've attached a minimal example with 2 Proteins ("GFP" and "MshA" (=A0A5P4S7Y3)) and 2 Groups ("D" & "F").

According to the log2 Intensities, we're expecting to see an upregulation of GFP in Group D and a  minus INF for MshA compared to Group FP:
  Protein                            D     F
1 sp|P42212|GFP_AEQVI             30.9  24.4
2 tr|A0A5P4S7Y3|A0A5P4S7Y3_VIBPH  NA    31.5

> comp_matrix <- MSstatsContrastMatrix("pairwise", c("D","F"))
       D  F
D vs F 1 -1

> DP_sel <- dataProcess(minimal_abc_sel)
> PW_sel <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix=comp_matrix, data=DP_sel, use_log_file = FALSE)
> PW_sel$ComparisonResult %>% select(Protein, Label, log2FC)
                         Protein  Label   log2FC
1            sp|P42212|GFP_AEQVI D vs F 6.443467
2 tr|A0A5P4S7Y3|A0A5P4S7Y3_VIBPH D vs F     -Inf

So far so good...

But if I repeat the whole analysis with swaped reference and sample group, this is what's happening:
> comp_matrix <- MSstatsContrastMatrix("pairwise", c("F","D"))
       F  D
F vs D 1 -1

> DP_sel <- dataProcess(minimal_abc_sel)
> PW_sel <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix=comp_matrix, data=DP_sel, use_log_file = FALSE)
> PW_sel$ComparisonResult %>% select(Protein, Label, log2FC)
                         Protein  Label    log2FC
1            sp|P42212|GFP_AEQVI F vs D -6.443467
2 tr|A0A5P4S7Y3|A0A5P4S7Y3_VIBPH F vs D      -Inf

Somehow the sign of the infinite regulation doesn't change here, although the regulation of GFP correctly switched from +6 fold up-regulation to -6 fold down-regulation...

I assume this observation has something to do with the default alphabetical ordering of group names in MSstatsContrastMatrix()...

Can you please have a look into this issue?

Thank you already in advance for your help!

Best,
Christian

PS: I've reproduced this observation with MSstats v.4.0.1, v.4.4.1, and v.4.5.1
